### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1697d5ca9ca45205583bf7d381a91b95bf2271f8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4588caea1c1cbaa7a2d4d8b8c5589aa7749582e6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/expression-refusal-codes.test.ts + packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/expression-refusal.ts, packages/cli/test/hook-timeout-override-refusal.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts, packages/formula/package.json, packages/formula/vitest.config.ts

Inputs read: card #30901 body and both comments (seat claim 6682594819, dev report 6683692239, read as claims); PR #30919 body, labels (`size/s`, `tests`, `skip-changeset`), file list and the net diff `origin/main...4588caea1c` fetched into a ref of my own (1 file, +43 −1, three commits on top of `origin/main` 6ff27b348e); the test file at `main` and at the head; the producers it calls; the Actions API read-only; the head's check-runs at 2026-11-06T11:33:57Z. The dispatch order and the dev's and seat's conclusions were not inputs to the verdict.

### ① Derived judgments

**(1) No weakened assertion — holds.** The key is `inspect(said, { depth: Infinity, breakLength: Infinity, maxArrayLength: Infinity, maxStringLength: Infinity })` over the whole refusal. `ExprValidationError` (`validate.ts` line 298) is `{ message, source } & ExpressionRefusal` = `{ code, params }`, and `refusal()` at line 316 is the single constructor, building exactly those four fields. The five assertions in the case read only `said.code`, `said.params` (typeof, not null, `Object.entries` values flattened by `paramStrings`), `said.message` and `said.source` (`expectLocatorsRead` reads `said.source.length`). All four are in the key; `inspect` at infinite depth tells `undefined` from absent, `NaN` from `null`, `-0` from `0`, and escapes strings injectively, so two refusals that differ in anything an assertion reads cannot share a key (key order differences split, never merge — the safe direction). `refusals++` runs before the `continue`, so every refusal is still counted and the `toBeGreaterThan(100)` control is unchanged; a duplicate's `code` equals the judged one's, so `provoked` still has to reach every code in `VALIDATE_CODES`. The three loops, `SWEEP_INPUTS` (40 sources x 3 spellings + 8 = 128, counted in the file) and `SWEEP_SCHEMAS` (15, counted) are untouched, so the case judges exactly the same 5,760 calls. The one thing the cut changes is diagnostic, not evidential: on a red, the `${said.code} from ${JSON.stringify(input)}` message names the first input that provoked that refusal rather than every one. Not a weakening.

**(2) The timeout — holds.** `VALIDATE_SWEEP_BUDGET_MS = 16_000` is passed as the `it()` third argument on the one case, not a `testTimeout` in `packages/formula/vitest.config.ts` (which carries none), and the diff adds no `.skip`, no `.retry`, no `retry:` option. Sizing follows the repo's per-case rule as `share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts` lines 90-93 state it and `hook-timeout-override-refusal.test.ts` lines 121-123 adopt it — 3x the slowest reading, rounded up to the next second: 3 x 5034 = 15102, so 16000. The reading is named with its run and job (`main` push run 42192379976, job 127808107135) and I read it in that job's log: `every refusal validateExpression reports on the sweep ... 5034ms`, `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.` at `expression-refusal-codes.test.ts:870:3`, the second sweep at 37 ms, the file at 5438 ms. The synchronous-body note is right: vitest judged the case after it returned, so 5034 is the whole run. The file-level 10 s rule (AGENTS.md, ruling record 6181973363) is not engaged — the file read 5.4 s in the failing job and the readings put it well under on an idle box. The 5034 reading is of the pre-cut case, so the budget is conservative for the post-cut body; the comment says to re-measure when inputs or schemas grow.

**(3) The measurement — holds on spot-check, with one honesty gap.** Spot-checked read-only against the Actions API:
- Job 127808107135: `Test Core (4/8)`, `main` push on d55acb7828, conclusion failure, the case at 5034 ms as above; the shard plan line in the same log reads `all bins: 1553/1556/1551/1552/1552/1553/1556/1554s`, as the body quotes.
- Shard walls on two cited push runs: 42181191624 — 1/8 1082 s, 2/8 407 s, 3/8 711 s, **4/8 1034 s**, 5/8 400 s, 6/8 567 s, 7/8 318 s, 8/8 726 s; 42136924584 — 1/8 1120 s, 2/8 464 s, 3/8 605 s, **4/8 1467 s**, 5/8 677 s, 6/8 512 s, 7/8 564 s, 8/8 733 s. Shard 4 slowest in both, shards 5-8 the fastest, consistent with the body's medians (4/8 1189 s vs 612-948 s).
- The failed-job census: the workflow is 224644133 (`ci.yml`); the window 2026-11-03T10:00Z to 2026-11-06T10:30Z now holds 324 push and 665 merge-group runs (the body's 320/660 were read an hour earlier; the drift is the window's live tail), 63 failed runs, exactly **29 failed `Test Core (N/8)` jobs**. Grepping each of the 29 logs: **10 carry `Test timed out in 5000ms` — 9 in `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` (all 4/8) and 1 the formula case**; 18 are `scripts/liveness/check-liveness.test.ts` assertion failures on 1/8 and 2/8; job 127654182380 (4/8) matches nothing — its log ends inside `verify`, as the body says. The body's numbers hold exactly.
- The near-5 s list: `cli unmanaged-tables.integration.test.ts › the boot this sweep reads from really did compose the deployment` read 3295 ms in run 42181191624, the table's max. The two `plugin-hono-server` rows were not in the run I read (that run did not execute hono-server) and stay the dev's reading, unverified here.
- Sample honesty: the body says "a sample of 7" for the CI case readings, "sample" for the 44-job case census, and names every query. One caveat it does not state (should-fix, below): run 42181191624, one of its six sampled push runs, planned **37 of 84 items** (shard 1/8 got 1 item), so the per-shard medians pool path-filtered push runs with full merge-group runs. The ranking survives — shard 4 is slowest in both runs I read — but the absolute medians are a mixed population.

**(4) Fixes honesty — stands on the card's own ownership clause, with two acts owed by the seat.** The card's Wanted says "rebalance the shards, cut the heavy work out of these cases, **and/or** set explicit per-case timeouts sized from the measurement, each with its reason", then "This card owns the measurement and the formula case." Both owned halves are in the tree and the PR body: the formula case carries a cut and a measured per-case budget with its reason, and the measurement (per-shard walls, the 29-job census, the 31-case default-5 s population) is in the body's acceptance notes with its queries. The shard plan is correctly not edited: `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` opens `GENERATED by scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs -- do not hand-edit`, `shard-timings-refresh.yml` runs on `cron: '30 5 * * 1'`, and the splitter's dataset was last carried on 2026-11-03 (4b71a82b76). What `Fixes #30901` does not close: the measured shard-4/8 overload (1.53x the mean median) and the nine near-5 s cases — the dev reports them under `out_of_scope_findings` with `carrier: seat to file` and `filed_issues: []`. Under Prime Directive #10 the two deterministic `plugin-hono-server` drain cases (4209 ms and 3230 ms on an idle box, every run, 84% and 65% of the default) are a reproducible defect, not a note. For Fixes to stand at close the seat files (a) the shard-4/8 readings onto #25870 (open, `pm:on-hold`, the card that owns re-deriving the cli slicing) or a fresh card if #25870 stays on hold, and (b) one class card for the default-5 s population led by the hono-server cases, and the PR body's acceptance notes name the carriers by number. Should-fix, not a FAIL: the acts are the seat's at ACCEPT and sit outside the tree, and the body already names them with a carrier.

**(5) The landing — holds.** `skip-changeset` is right: `@objectstack/formula` publishes `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]`, the diff touches one `src/*.test.ts`, and `Check Changeset` is green. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in the body and match a test-only diff. The body matches the tree: one file, `+43 −1`, `inspect` import, `refusalKey`, `VALIDATE_SWEEP_BUDGET_MS` with its comment, `judged` set, the budget as third argument; "no global `testTimeout`, no skip, no retry" is true of the diff and of the formula vitest config. The diff stays out of `packages/rest` and `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts`. No governed path, no `packages/spec`, head repo is the base repo (not a fork), PR is draft and bot-authored for the owning seat to land. `node:util` is a builtin and two other formula tests already import `node:` modules.

**Check-runs on the head at 2026-11-06T11:33:57Z** — the gate verdicts, some still running: success — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, every completed `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` lane; skipped — `Lint UI` (path filter); **in progress** — `Test Core (1/8)` through `(8/8)`, `Test UI (1/16)` through `(16/16)`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`. `Test Core` reruns the formula suite and is the one that re-measures this case; the PASS below is on the tree and does not stand in for its conclusion.

### ② Semver level

None. A test-only diff in `packages/formula/src`; nothing the package publishes moves. `skip-changeset` holds; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Governed surfaces: none touched (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/workflows/**`).
- `packages/spec`: untouched; no generated artifact owed.
- Out of this card's lane and untouched, as ordered: `packages/rest` (#30873), `packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` (#30785), `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` and the splitter (#25870, generator-owned).
- Production code in the clocked window: `buildTypedEnv` (`cel-engine.ts` line 965, "Built per call") is the sweep's cost centre and is not changed; the body names the memoisation as an observation, not filed. Fine for this card.
- Fork: no — head repo `objectstack-ai/objectstack`.

### ④ Design judgment

The change holds against the code it cites. `refusalKey` is sound because the refusal is a plain four-field value object built in exactly one place and every assertion is a pure function of that object; the dedup is a memo of a deterministic verdict, not a filter on what is judged. The budget is sized and documented to the repo's own per-case rule and pinned to a named CI reading, placed on the one case, and the second sweep (5-37 ms) is rightly left on the default. The two readings that are counts without a tree (should-fix 1) are the only drift from the house standard "a reading is a count plus the tree it was taken against".

**Must-fix:** none.

**Should-fix:**
1. `expression-refusal-codes.test.ts` — the in-case comment "The sweep's 3,865 refusals are 199 distinct ones" and the budget comment's "Other `Test Core` jobs of the same three days: 429 to 3065" are readings with no tree and no sample size: name the commit the counts were taken on (the body's `98f640d581`) and say the 429-3065 band is seven jobs, or drop the numbers. The structural counts (5,760 = 3 x 128 x 15) are fine — they are the file's own arrays.
2. PR body, acceptance notes — state that the per-shard medians pool path-filtered `main` push runs (run 42181191624 planned 37 of 84 items) with full merge-group runs, or restrict the table to full-plan runs, before #25870 re-derives the cli slicing from it.
3. For `Fixes #30901` to stand at close, the seat files the two carriers the dev report leaves to it — the shard-4/8 overload onto #25870 (or a fresh card while it is on hold) and one class card for the default-5 s population led by the two deterministic `plugin-hono-server` drain cases (a PD #10 reproducible defect, noted but unfiled) — and the body names them by number.
